newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher sees small group in EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher sees small group in EMU in 1999.

text.p: European Economic and Monetary Union should probably start with a small group of nations rather than be delayed in the hope of gathering more member countries, a Bundesbank council member said on Tuesday.

Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher, president of the regional central bank in Berlin, said in a speech to a business forum in Berlin that there was no guarantee economic convergence between participating countries would be improved if EMU were delayed.
It would be equally unwise to start monetary union at any cost by relaxing the entry criteria to allow more countries in, he said according to the text of a speech released in advance.
"It would therefore be sensible to start with a small group," he said.
Countries which want to join European monetary union must meet goals on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budgets and public borrowing in the crunch 1997 year.

Entering a debate as to whether countries have to actually be members of the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) to meet the terms of the Maastricht Treaty, Kuehbacher said that the five nations currently not in the ERM did not meet the exchange rate criterion for entry.
Some countries have argued ERM membership is not an essential prerequisite for joining EMU providing a currency's exchange rate has been stable for some time.
"There are still considerable problems in meeting the exchange rate criterion," Kuehbacher said.
"Five EU member countries are currently not taking part in the ERM exchange rate mechanism and therefore do not meet the relevant criterion from the start," he said.
He added, without elaborating, that the peseta and the escudo had also been develued within the system in March 1995.
